key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of perovskites from early time-series data, enabling faster stability assessment.
engineering_relevance: This approach could reduce the time and cost of accelerated ageing tests for perovskite solar materials while improving interpretability of stability predictions.
method: Collected 167 metal halide perovskite samples spanning different compositions and crystallinities.
Recorded heat/light stress experiments with more than 86,000 photoluminescence spectra.
Used physics-informed featurization plus a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity for unseen samples.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on unseen materials and reportedly outperformed baseline benchmarks while generalizing across material groups.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and representativeness of the stress-test dataset, so broader deployment will need validation across additional perovskite chemistries and operating conditions.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
